questions.knowledge_point: Identifying a Possible Curve Given Its Arc Length As an Integral
questions.problem: The length of a curve $y=f(x)$ is given by ${\int }_{3}^{5}\sqrt{1+25{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x.$ Which of the following could be  an equation for this curve?
questions.worked_solution:
The arc length of a curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=a$ and $x=b$ can be found using the formula

$$
L={\int }_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We're given that 

$$
L={\int }_{3}^{5}\sqrt{1+25{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Comparing the above with the arc length formula, we see that we must have

$$
[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}=25{x}^{4}\,⟹\,{f}^{′}(x)=\pm 5{x}^{2}.
$$

Integrating the above equation with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\pm 5\int {x}^{2}\text{ d}x \\  & =\pm \frac{5}{3}{x}^{3}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given options, the only one that has the required form is $y=-\frac{5}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{11}{3}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Arc Length of a Smooth Curve Using the Arc Length Formula
questions.problem: Compute the arc length of $y=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}$ for $x\in [\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},1].$
questions.worked_solution:
The arc length of a curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=a$ and $x=b$ can be found using the formula

$$
L={\int }_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}},$ $a=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ and $b=1.$

First, we find the derivative of $f(x):$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}
$$

Now, let's compute $\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}} & =\sqrt{1+{(-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+\frac{{x}^{2}}{1-{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1-{x}^{2}+{x}^{2}}{1-{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}$ to the formula for the arc length, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{\sqrt{2}/2}^{1}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\sqrt{2}/2}^{1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x){|}_{\sqrt{2}/2}^{1} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Arc Length of a Smooth Curve Using the Arc Length Formula
questions.problem: Compute the arc length of $y=\frac{2}{3}{(1+{x}^{2})}^{3/2}$ for $x\in [0,3].$
questions.worked_solution:
The arc length of a curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=a$ and $x=b$ can be found using the formula

$$
L={\int }_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=\frac{2}{3}{(1+{x}^{2})}^{3/2},$ $a=0,$ and $b=3.$

First, we find the derivative of $f(x):$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}{(1+{x}^{2})}^{1/2}\cdot 2x=2x\sqrt{(1+{x}^{2})}
$$

Now, let's compute $\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}} & =\sqrt{1+{[2x\sqrt{(1+{x}^{2})}]}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4{x}^{2}+4{x}^{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{(2{x}^{2}+1)^{2}} \\  & =2{x}^{2}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}=2{x}^{2}+1$ to the formula for the arc length, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(2{x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}+x)|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =[\frac{2}{3}(3)^{3}+(3)]-[\frac{2}{3}(0)^{3}+(0)] \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The length of a curve $y=f(x)$ is given by ${\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{(2-x)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.$ Which of the following could be  an equation for this curve?
questions.worked_solution:
The arc length of a curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=a$ and $x=b$ can be found using the formula

$$
L={\int }_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We're given that 

$$
L={\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{(2-x)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Comparing the above with the arc length formula, we see that we must have

$$
[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}=\frac{1}{(2-x)^{2}}\,⟹\,{f}^{′}(x)=\pm \frac{1}{2-x}.
$$

Integrating the above equation with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\pm \int \frac{1}{2-x}\text{ d}x \\  & =\pm (-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2-x))+C \\  & =∓\operatorname{ln}⁡(2-x)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given options, the only one that has the required form is $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2-x)+1.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Arc Length of a Smooth Curve Using the Arc Length Formula
questions.worked_solution:
The arc length of a curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=a$ and $x=b$ can be found using the formula

$$
L={\int }_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}+\operatorname{arccos}⁡x,$ $a=0,$ and $b=1.$

First, we find the derivative of $f(x):$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}=-\frac{1+x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}
$$

Now, let's compute $\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}} & =\sqrt{1+{(-\frac{1+x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+\frac{(1+x)^{2}}{1-{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1-{x}^{2}+1+2x+{x}^{2}}{1-{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2+2x}{1-{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2(1+x)}{(1-x)(1+x)}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2}{1-x}}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{1-x}}$ into the arc length formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{\frac{2}{1-x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{1-x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\sqrt{2}\sqrt{1-x}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-2\sqrt{2}\sqrt{1-1}-(-2\sqrt{2}\sqrt{1-0}) \\  & =0-(-2\sqrt{2}) \\  & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
